text:
Steven Horsford addresses tariffs, gaming regulation, and nuclear waste policy for Nevada
Rep. Steven Horsford, U.S. Congressman representing Nevada’s 4th district since 2019, has used his social media platform to address several policy issues affecting both Nevada and the nation in recent days.
On July 26, Horsford criticized the Trump administration's approach to tariffs, stating, "The Supreme Court already struck down President Trump’s first round of tariffs. Instead of racing to create new tariffs under a different legal excuse, we should be focused on giving relief to the families and small businesses that have already lost money. Nevadans paid the price".
The following day, he commented on Nevada's gaming industry regulations: "Nevada’s gaming economy works because there are rules, regulators, and real accountability behind it. That system protects consumers, supports workers, and gives people confidence that gaming is being done the right way. Prediction markets are trying to blur the line and operate".
Later on July 27, Horsford reiterated his opposition to nuclear waste storage in Nevada by addressing federal policymakers, "A reminder to the Trump administration, Nevada has not been and will never be the nation’s nuclear dumping ground. Hard stop."
Steven Horsford was born in Las Vegas in 1973 and continues to reside there at age 49. He holds a BA from the University of Nevada, Reno (FACTS 1-4). Before joining Congress in 2019—replacing Ruben Kihuen—he served in the Nevada Senate from 2009 to 2013.
